anya: FYI brought up Odo-11B (baseline fp16) on the test fleet today. Quick econ + quality smoke notes below.

jordan: nice — did you try int6 quant yet?

anya: yes. Ran int6 and int8 quant configs across chat and completion slices. Short summary first: int6 ~= 2.5x token cost reduction vs fp16, median latency +8ms on our 4090 nodes, and an average GTN signal drop of ~1.2% (multi-turn chat).

liam: can you paste the slice numbers?

anya: paste below (short):
- sample size: 5k multi-turn chat sessions, 3k single-turn completions
- fp16 P50/P95 latency (4090): 52ms / 190ms
- int8 P50/P95 latency: 56ms / 195ms
- int6 P50/P95 latency: 60ms / 210ms
- relative token cost (per 1M tokens): fp16 = $4.8k, int8 = $2.4k, int6 = $1.9k
- GTN quality delta (paired eval): fp16 baseline, int8 = -0.4% (insignificant), int6 = -1.2% (small but consistent on long-form summarization)

sunil: interesting. Where do failures/regressions show up?

anya: mostly on long-context reference resolution and rare factuality cases; short Q&A and routing tasks are fine. Example: prompts with >2k tokens context, int6 sometimes drops entity recall ~3-4% on our extractive metric.

jordan: any latency tail issues? P99s?

anya: p99 numbers: fp16 420ms, int8 440ms, int6 520ms on our synthetic burst test. Tail increases due to KV cache pack fragmentation and slightly higher compute per step at higher token lengths.

liam: ops question — does int6 require different batching/cache tuning?

anya: yes: recommended config changes for int6 in test profile: reduce max_batch_wait_ms from 8->6 for chat endpoints, enable prefix KV cache aggressively for repeated conversations, and set kvcache_shard_size to 64MB (was 128MB for fp16). That reduces p95 by ~10-12% in our runs.

sunil: ok econ for product/GTN: what should we recommend?

anya: proposal:
1) GTN primary chat route: int8 (good cost win, negligible quality change).
2) GTN long-form / high-fidelity paths: keep fp16 or int8 fallback for contexts > 1.5k tokens.
3) Experimental low-cost route: int6 as canary on <20% traffic for non-critical completions (saves ~60% vs fp16).
4) Add automatic rollback if GTN quality signal drops >1.5% in 1h window.

jordan: makes sense. Any A/B test design suggestions?

anya: A/B: run 10% traffic to int6 for 2 weeks, measure: user satisfaction proxy (CTR on suggestions), completion acceptance rate, GTN eval score, and token-econ delta. If quality delta <1% overall and product metrics stable, increase to 40%.

liam: ops notes for Dedicated customers?

anya: Dedicated: recommend initial offering as int8 default; allow customers to opt into int6 with a warning about edge-case fidelity. For reserved pools, add an opt-in knob in console with a per-model QC flag.

deploy-bot: Deploy summary: odo-11b-fp16 test fleet green. int8 canary deployed -> 2026-03-21T18:05Z. int6 canary queued.

sunil: thanks. Can you produce a one-pager scorecard for GTN with thresholds we can embed in the runbook?

anya: will do — quick scorecard draft:
- Primary metric: GTN eval score (higher == better)
- Acceptable deltas: int8: <= 0.5% drop, int6: <= 1.5% drop for non-critical slices
- Latency budget: P95 <= 220ms for chat routes; P99 alert if >500ms
- Unit econ target: reduce per-token cost >=2x vs fp16 for Tier-A routes to consider quantization
- Auto-rollout condition: quality delta < threshold for 24h and no production incidents

jordan: embarassingly practical — throw that into a short doc and ping product.

anya: done, will upload a short doc and include sample eval notebook + plots. Link (placeholder): https://redwood.internal/eng-ml/odo11b-int6-econ-smoke 

liam: experimental note: also tried hybrid routing (int6 for causal prefix, int8 for final decode). It cuts cost ~2.1x and quality loss is only -0.6%. Worth a pilot.

sunil: ok let's run hybrid pilot on low-risk completion routes. Jordan/Anya, coordinate with GTN eng to add metric hooks.

anya: will set up slices + GTN hooks today, tagging you both shortly. :rocket:

jordan: thx — appreciate the fast turnaround.

liam: +1 on hybrid pilot.

sunil: closing: recommendation summary for product/GTN -> int8 primary, int6 for limited non-critical traffic and hybrid routing as promising middle ground. Action items: anya to upload scorecard + notebook, jordan to prep GTN experiment, liam to schedule hybrid canary.

anya: noted, will follow up in a doc and with PR for canaries.
